identity.name: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C)
identity.chemical_class: Water-soluble vitamin (ascorbate) and antioxidant organic acid (lactone)

function.mechanism: Acts as a reducing agent/electron donor, limiting oxidation reactions in food matrices.
common_food_categories: general processed foods requiring oxidation control

adi.basis: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation indicated no need for a numerical ADI.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no safety concern at reported uses and use levels for E300/E301/E302 and no numerical ADI was needed.

adi.basis: JECFA lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED (group ADI for ascorbic acid and sodium/potassium/calcium salts).

concerns.summary: Kidney stone and oxalate-related risk signals are mainly reported at high supplemental or IV doses (often around or above 1,000 mg/day), rather than normal additive exposure.
key_references: Total, Dietary, and Supplemental Vitamin C Intake and Risk of Incident Kidney Stones (2016)
Ascorbic Acid Supplements and Kidney Stones Incidence Among Men and Women: A systematic review and meta-analysis (2019)
Harm of IV High-Dose Vitamin C Therapy in Adult Patients: A Scoping Review (2020)

concerns.summary: High-dose IV contexts have reported adverse-event concerns including hemolysis risk in G6PD deficiency and glucometer interference.
key_references: Harm of IV High-Dose Vitamin C Therapy in Adult Patients: A Scoping Review (2020)

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation reported no safety concern at reported food-additive use levels and no need for a numerical ADI.
JECFA lists ADI as not specified for ascorbic acid group.

populations: No specific ADI exceedance group identified for normal food-additive exposure
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA/JECFA use a non-numeric ADI framework (not specified/no numerical ADI). Risk concerns arise mainly in high-dose supplement or therapeutic settings.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory authorities (EFSA, FDA, JECFA) support use with no numerical ADI/ADI not specified and no major concern at food-additive levels; adverse findings are mostly limited to high-dose supplemental or IV exposure contexts.
key_factors: EFSA 2015 no numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses
FDA GRAS status under 21 CFR 182.3013 with GMP condition
Renal adverse signals concentrate at high-dose non-additive exposures
